sentences.text:
Challenging common judgment and separate awards dated 14.07.2016 passed by Member,
MACT-VII, Vijaypur (for short 'tribunal') in MVC nos.260/2013 and 263/2013, these appeals are filed.

2. Sri Sanganagouda V. Biradar, learned counsel for appellants submitted that appeals were by claimants seeking for enhancement of compensation as well as challenging finding of tribunal regarding contributory negligence.

It was submitted that on 05.12.2012 at 9.30 p.m. Hanamant was riding motorcycle bearing Reg. no.KA- NC: 2023:KHC-K:7491 28/EB-1318 from Horti towards Vijayapur when a lorry bearing registration no.CG-07/CA-9870 was wrongly parked on road without any precautionary measures,
consequently, motorcycle of Hanmanth dashed against lorry and caused accident.

In said accident,
he sustained fatal injuries and died on spot.
3. Claiming compensation for same, claim petition was filed by his mother and siblings against owner and insurer of lorry.
Despite service of notice, owner did not appear and contest.

He was placed ex-parte.
4.
Only insurer filed objection opposing claim petition on all grounds.
It was specifically contended that accident occurred due to sole negligence of rider of motorcycle as lorry was parked on left side.
While admitting issuance of insurance policy, violation of terms and conditions were contended.

sentences.text: Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant no.1 was examined as PW.1 and three others were examined as PWs.2 to 4.
Exs . P.1
to P.21 were got marked.

For respondents, official of insurer was examined as RW.1 and copy of insurance policy was got marked as Ex.R1.
5.
On consideration, tribunal held that accident had occurred due to negligence of both rider of motorcycle as well as driver of lorry in equal extent and apportioned negligence at 50% each.
It assessed total compensation of `9,29,000/- in MVC no.206/2013 and `10,000/- in MVC no.263/2013.

Assailing same, it was submitted that admittedly, finding of tribunal regarding contributory negligence was based on prosecution records which were initiated on basis of complaint filed by brother of deceased who was not an eyewitness.
It was further submitted that parking of lorry on road would be per se violation of Road Regulations, 1989.

Since Regulation 15 of Road Regulation permitted parking subject to taking all precautions and since no precautions were taken and vehicle parked being a heavy goods vehicle, entire negligence was required to be fastened on lorry driver.
On quantum in MFA no.200106/2017 - it was submitted that deceased Hanumanth was 33 years of age and had passed BA., B.Ed., and MA examinations.
He had appeared for competitive recruitment examinations.
It was submitted that even notional income for year 2012 in case of ordinary coolie would be `6,500/- and therefore sought for consideration of higher amount than same as monthly income of deceased.
It was further submitted that tribunal had erred in not adding future prospects and award under conventional heads also required enhancement.
7. In MFA no.200107/2021 : It was submitted that in above mentioned accident that motorcycle belonging to Changond involved in accident was severely damaged.
A sum of `51,590/- was spent towards its repairs.

Though bills were produced, tribunal awarded meager extent of `20,000/-
towards same, which called for enhancement.

8. It was also submitted that said lorry was found parked at accident spot even upto four days after instant accident and on 09.12.2012, another vehicle dashed NC: 2023:KHC-K:7491 against said lorry and in respect of subsequent accident, FIR was registered only against said lorry driver for negligent parking of vehicle on road.
9.
On other hand, Shri S.S.Aspalli learned counsel for respondent/insurer sought to support award.
It was submitted that criminal prosecution was set in motion by none other than brother of deceased who filed FIR alleging rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by deceased himself.
Based on same, abated charge-sheet was registered.
Since vehicle was parked by side of road, there was no ground for interference with apportionment of contributory negligence.
Insofar as enhancement, it was submitted that tribunal on consideration of material on record had passed just award and no enhancement was called for.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for parties.

Perused impugned judgment and award as well as record.
11.
From above submission and since claimants are in appeal challenging finding of tribunal on contributory NC: 2023:KHC-K:7491 negligence and seeking for enhancement of compensation,
points
that arise for consideration are "(i) Whether finding of tribunal regarding contributory negligence calls for interference ?
(ii) Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation ?"

Point no.(i) :
12.

To establish actionable negligence against respondents, claimant relied upon FIR, Complaint,
Spot Panchanama, Motor Vehicles Inspector's Report and also FIR and Charge-sheet marked as Exs.P1 to P.3, Exs.P.6, P7 and P.20 and P.21 respectively.
Perusal of Ex.P.1 - FIR would indicate that it is based on complaint given by brother of deceased.

In Ex.P.2-complaint it is specifically contended that after receiving information about his brother on his motorcycle meeting with accident, he visited accident spot and after seeing it, filed complaint.
In complaint, it is specifically stated that motorcycle dashed against lorry parked by side of road.
Ex . P.3

-spot NC:
2023:KHC-K:7491 panchanama, does not describe the exact location of accident spot or about manner of parking of lorry.

Exs . P.20 and P.21 are FIR and charge-sheet registered against driver of very same lorry for causing another accident by negligent parking of vehicle at accident spot subsequent to accident in consideration.

If lorry driver was negligent in case of subsequent accident,
then he canot be completely absolved in earlier case.
13.

In view of above two factors, finding of tribunal apportioning negligence against lorry driver and deceased at 50% each would appear just and proper especially taking note of obligation of drivers parking their vehicles on road to take precautions and other drivers to maintain safe distance.
Hence, point no.(i) is answered in negative.
Point no.(ii) :

14. In MFA no.200106/2017 though claimants stated that deceased had passed B.A., B.Ed., and M.A examinations and appeared for competitive examinations, awaiting results, except producing marks cards, there is - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7491 no material placed to substantiate same.
In absence, tribunal would be justified in assessing monthly income of deceased notionally.
Notional income in case of ordinary person for year 2012 would be `6,500/-.
Since deceased was post graduate, it would be proper to consider his earning capacity at `9,000/-.
Claimants are mother and siblings.
While assessing compensation, tribunal has deducted 1/4th towards personal expenses and applied multiplier of '16'.
As per ratio in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others1, claimants would be entitled for addition of 40% of income towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, compensation towards 'loss of dependency' would be `18,14,400/- [(`9,000 + 40%) X  X 12 X 16].

sentences.text: To said amount, amount of `77,000/- under conventional heads has to be added as per Pranay Sethi's case (supra) (70,000+10%).
Thus, total (2017) 16 SCC 680 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7491 compensation would be `18,91,400/-.
Point no.(ii) is answered partly in affirmative as above.
16. In MFA no.200106/2017 - Appeal is filed against award towards vehicle damages.

To substantiate same, claimant produced original Registration Certificate as Ex.P.19, Bills issued by Diamond Automobiles for `33,221/- Ex.P.17 and Estimate issued by Patil Automotives for `51,590/-
Ex.P.18.

Taking note of claim by petitioner for `35,000/- i.e., `25,000/- towards vehicle damages and `10,000/- towards non-availability of vehicle, tribunal has disbelieved bills and awarded lump- sum compensation of `20,000/-.
17. Merely on ground of claim being lesser than entitlement, would not hold hands of tribunal in granting higher sum.
However as rightly observed by tribunal, Ex.P.18 is estimate while Ex.P.17 are bills totaling to `33,221/-.
Considering same, tribunal ought to have awarded `35,000/- towards vehicle damages.
Thus, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.
It is - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7491 held that claimant would be entitled for `35,000/- towards vehicle damages.
Consequently, following :
ORDER (i) Appeals are allowed in part.

(ii) Claimant in MFA no.200107/2017 is held entitled for total compensation of `35,000/-
and claimants in MFA no.200106/2017 are held entitled for total compensation of `18,91,400/-with interest at 6% p.a. from date of claim petition till deposit.
(iii) Insurer would be liable to pay 50% of same i.e., at `9,45,700/- and `17,500/- which shall be deposited within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.

(iv) Insofar as apportionment - on deposit, it is held that 75% of award amount shall be apportioned in favour of claimant no.1- mother with liberty is reserved to her to - 13 - Kallawwa And Ors vs Dharamveer Choudary And Anr
